name: David Paul
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2024)
forbes_bio: David C. Paul is the founder and executive chairman of spine implant manufacturer Globus Medical.
A mechanical engineer by training, Paul moved to the U.S. from India to get his master's degree at Temple University.
Paul worked as an engineer for medical device giant Synthes before leaving in 2003 to start Globus.
Paul took Globus public in 2012.
In 2017 Paul stepped down as CEO due to a "health condition," according to a company press release.
forbes_facts: Globus makes the Excelsius GPS, one of the only spinal surgery robots on the market today.

name: Liu Zhongtian
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2010-2022); Hurun Global (2014-2021); Hurun China (2003-2020)
forbes_bio: Liu Zhongtian is the founder of Hong Kong-listed aluminum products manufacturer China Zhongwang Holdings.
Liu resigned as the chairman of China Zhongwang due to "personal health reasons" in November 2017.
Zhongwang USA, majority owned by Wang, ended a deal to buy aluminum processor Aleris in November 2017, citing U.S. regulatory uncertainty.
In September 2016, Liu denied reports that his company might be dodging U.S. tariffs by storing a reported 6% of the world's aluminum in Mexico.

name: Sebastian Kulczyk
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Sebastian Kulczyk and his sister Dominika Kulczyk inherited a fortune from their father Jan, who died in 2015 from complications of minor heart surgery.
In 2018, the siblings divvied up assets, with Sebastian getting a stake in Autostrada Eksploatacja, which maintains a major highway.
He also took over the chemical business Ciech and shares in mining companies, the latter of which he sold. He took Ciech private in 2024, renaming it Qemetica.
Sebastian also founded and runs VC tech fund Manta Ray.
forbes_facts: Sebastian Kulczyk worked in the digital media unit at Sony BMG in New York when he was 21.

Early in his career, Lee was involved in auto-parts trading.

name: Agustín Coppel Luken
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Agustín Coppel Luken is the chairman and CEO of Mexican retail and banking giant Grupo Coppel.
The Coppel family owns 100% of the $8 billion-plus (sales) company which their father founded in Sinaloa in 1941.
The stores, known for providing credit to customers, started allowing buyers to pay in weekly installments after World War II.
In 2024, the group announced it would invest over $700 million renovating existing retailers, reducing its carbon footprint and opening over 100 new stores.
The company was reportedly exploring a more than $1 billion IPO in 2018 but the plans were indefinitely postponed.
forbes_facts: Agustín and his wife are avid collectors of contemporary art.

name: He Zhaoxi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026); Hurun China (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: He Zhaoxi is the chairman of Sangfor Technologies, a supplier of IT infrastructure solutions.
The company went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2018.
He graduated from China University of Science and Technology in 1998 with a degree in automatic control and economic management.
After graduating, He worked for Huawei Technologies from 1998 to 2000.
He cofounded Sangfor Technologies in 2000.

name: Karl Hedin
forbes_bio: Karl Hedin is the owner of AB Karl Hedin, a Swedish timber group in sawmills, building materials and forestry.
The company was founded by Hedin's grandfather in 1937 and is now a leading player in Sweden's forest industry.
Hedin is known for his strong views on forest ownership and has criticized Swedish environmental policy.
In March 2025, Hedin announced plans to sell the group's sawmills and packaging division.
